items.title: 68436_Alberta Hunter oral history interview
items.q: And in there comes Sophie Tucker, and all the big shows from downtown -- the big stars would come up.

ctx.x: I went up to the Panama. That's at 35th and State. Up there was Nellie Carr, Twinkle Davis, Goldie Crosby, Lord have mercy, what's that other girl's name? Another girl and myself. I'll think of her name, because I want her to be in there. And we was the hot shots, upstairs, you know. And the people used to pass off like Brick, Cora Green, Mattie Wright, Nellie Compton and Florence Mills. They'd come upstairs to hear us, because downstairs was the swing, and we were the blues, upstairs. See, they'd come upstairs…

And I would sing the blues. And in there comes Sophie Tucker, and all the big shows from downtown -- the big stars would come up. But they'd come upstairs to hear us. And then I -- well, I became so popular that everybody was trying to get me then, you know. And then I went -- I think I went next door to Frank Peer's Deluxe. And that's where Freddie Keppard was.

Oh, in the meantime, upstairs in the Panama was a piano player named George Hall. He was magnificent. He was wonderful, George Hall. His name was George Hall. And he played some piano. And the musicians used to come up to hear him play piano.
